source.text: זֶ֣ה סֵ֔פֶר תּוֹלְדֹ֖ת אָדָ֑ם בְּי֗וֹם בְּרֹ֤א אֱלֹהִים֙ אָדָ֔ם בִּדְמ֥וּת אֱלֹהִ֖ים עָשָׂ֥ה אֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is the] book of [the] generations of Adam. In [the] day of God's creating humankind, in [the] likeness of God he made him.

en.L: This [is] the book of the generations of Adam. In the day God created {{gender:humankind|man}}, in the likeness of God {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: This is the written account of Adam's family line. When God created {{gender:human beings|man}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them in the likeness of God.
en.R: This is the list of Adam's family. When God created {{gender:people|man}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them to be like God.

es.L: Este [es] el libro de las generaciones de Adán. En el día en que Dios creó {{gender:a los seres humanos|al hombre}}, a semejanza de Dios {{gender:los|lo}} hizo.
es.B: Este es el registro escrito de la descendencia de Adán. Cuando Dios creó {{gender:a los seres humanos|al hombre}}, {{gender:los|lo}} hizo a semejanza de Dios.
es.R: Esta es la lista de la familia de Adán. Cuando Dios creó {{gender:a las personas|al hombre}}, {{gender:las hizo parecidas|lo hizo parecido}} a Dios.

fr.L: Ceci [est] le livre des générations d’Adam. Au jour où Dieu créa {{gender:l’humanité|l’homme}}, à la ressemblance de Dieu {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{gender:la|le}} fit.
fr.B: Voici le récit écrit de la descendance d’Adam. Lorsque Dieu créa {{gender:les êtres humains|l’homme}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{gender:les fit|le fit}} à la ressemblance de Dieu.
fr.R: Voici la liste de la famille d’Adam. Quand Dieu a créé {{gender:les humains|l’homme}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{gender:les a faits semblables|l’a fait semblable}} à Dieu.

sw.L: Hiki [ni] kitabu cha vizazi vya Adamu. Siku ile Mungu alipowaumba wanadamu, aliwafanya kwa mfano wa Mungu.
sw.B: Hii ni kumbukumbu iliyoandikwa ya ukoo wa Adamu. Mungu alipowaumba wanadamu, aliwafanya kwa mfano wa Mungu.
sw.R: Hii ni orodha ya jamaa ya Adamu. Mungu alipowaumba watu, aliwafanya wafanane {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.

decisions.choice: the book of the generations: a written record of the family line
decisions.reason: "Book" means any written document, here a written list. "Generations" is the heading word of 2:4 and of each new section of Genesis; here it introduces Adam's descendants through Seth, down to Noah.

decisions.choice: Adam ... humankind: the same word as a name and as humankind
decisions.reason: The verse uses the word twice: first as the name of the first man, then, as in 1:26-27, for humankind. The list begins by going back to creation.

decisions.choice: in the likeness of God he made them: the words of 1:26-27
decisions.reason: The genealogy opens by repeating chapter 1: humankind made in God's likeness, male and female, blessed and named (verse 2). Whatever has happened in chapters 3-4, this is still what human beings are.

decisions.choice: humankind / human beings / people, and them; with the traditional setting, man and him
decisions.reason: As in 1:26-27: the word means human beings of both sexes, so the default is inclusive; the gender setting gives the traditional "man" and the Hebrew singular "him".

decisions.choice: a los seres humanos (L, B) / a las personas (R), with "los" / "las"; with the traditional setting, "al hombre" and "lo"
decisions.reason: As in English: the word means human beings of both sexes, so the default is inclusive and plural; the gender setting gives the traditional singular "al hombre ... lo". Spanish puts the object pronoun (and at Readable the agreeing adjective, "parecidas" / "parecido") inside the span so that it agrees with the noun chosen.

decisions.choice: passé simple (L, B); passé composé (R)
decisions.reason: French narrative tense by level, as the French style guide sets it: the passé simple of written narrative at Literal and Balanced ("créa", "vécut", "engendra"), the passé composé of spoken French at Readable ("a créé", "a vécu").

decisions.choice: {{gender:l’humanité|l’homme}} (L), {{gender:les êtres humains|l’homme}} (B), {{gender:les humains|l’homme}} (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: the word means human beings of both sexes, so the default is inclusive and the gender setting gives the traditional "l'homme". The pronoun and the verb that agree with the noun ("la", "les fit", "les a faits semblables") are under the same setting, so each option reads as one sentence.

decisions.choice: wanadamu (L, B), watu (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Swahili "wanadamu" and "watu" already mean human beings of both sexes, and the only "traditional" alternative, "wanaume", would mean males and change the meaning, so the Swahili has no gender span here or in verse 2 (style guide). The plural follows the English default "them".

source.text: זָכָ֥ר וּנְקֵבָ֖ה בְּרָאָ֑ם וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֹתָ֗ם וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֶת־שְׁמָם֙ אָדָ֔ם בְּי֖וֹם הִבָּֽרְאָֽם׃ס

en.L: Male and female {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} created them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} blessed them and called their name {{gender:Humankind|Man}} in the day they were created.

en.R: He made them male and female. He blessed them and gave them the name {{gender:Human|Man}} on the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them.

es.L: Varón y hembra los creó, y los bendijo, y llamó su nombre {{gender:Humanidad|Hombre}} en el día en que fueron creados.

es.R: Los hizo hombre y mujer. Los bendijo y les puso el nombre de {{gender:Humanidad|Hombre}} el día en que los hizo.

fr.L: Mâle et femelle {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les créa ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les bénit et appela leur nom {{gender:Humanité|Homme}} au jour où ils furent créés.

fr.R: Il les a faits homme et femme. Il les a bénis et leur a donné le nom d’{{gender:Humain|Homme}} le jour où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a faits.

sw.L: Mwanamume na mwanamke aliwaumba, akawabariki, akawaita jina lao Mwanadamu siku ile walipoumbwa.
sw.B: Aliwaumba mwanamume na mwanamke. Akawabariki, akawaita Mwanadamu walipoumbwa.
sw.R: Aliwafanya mwanamume na mwanamke. Akawabariki, akawapa jina Mwanadamu siku ile alipowafanya.

decisions.choice: called their name humankind: a name for man and woman together
decisions.reason: God gives the name adam to both, male and female together: it is the name of the human race, as well as of its first man (verse 3).

decisions.choice: Humankind (Human at Readable); with the traditional setting, Man
decisions.reason: The name given to both is the word for humankind (m1), capitalised as a name.

decisions.choice: Humanidad at every level; with the traditional setting, Hombre
decisions.reason: English Readable says "Human"; as a name in Spanish "Humano" sounds odd, and "Humanidad" is already a plain word, so Spanish keeps it at Readable too (m1: one name for man and woman together).

source.text: וַֽיְחִ֣י אָדָ֗ם שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּמְאַת֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד בִּדְמוּת֖וֹ כְּצַלְמ֑וֹ וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ שֵֽׁת׃

records.literal_gloss: And lived Adam thirty and a hundred year[s], and he fathered in his likeness, according to his image, and called his name Seth.

en.L: And Adam lived 130 years and fathered [a son] in his likeness, according to his image, and called his name Seth.
en.B: When Adam had lived 130 years, he had a son in his own likeness, in his own image, and he named him Seth.
en.R: When Adam was 130 years old, he had a son who was like him, and he named him Seth.

es.L: Y vivió Adán 130 años y engendró [un hijo] en su semejanza, según su imagen, y le dio el nombre de Set.
es.B: Cuando Adán había vivido 130 años, tuvo un hijo a su propia semejanza y a su propia imagen, y le puso por nombre Set.
es.R: Cuando Adán tenía 130 años, tuvo un hijo que se parecía a él, y lo llamó Set.

fr.L: Et Adam vécut 130 ans et engendra [un fils] à sa ressemblance, selon son image, et il appela son nom Seth.
fr.B: Lorsqu’Adam eut vécu 130 ans, il eut un fils à sa propre ressemblance, à sa propre image, et il l’appela Seth.
fr.R: Quand Adam avait 130 ans, il a eu un fils qui lui ressemblait, et il l’a appelé Seth.

sw.L: Naye Adamu akaishi miaka 130, akazaa [mwana] kwa mfano wake, kwa sura yake, akamwita jina lake Sethi.
sw.B: Adamu alipokuwa ameishi miaka 130, alipata mwana aliyefanana naye, kwa sura yake mwenyewe, akamwita Sethi.
sw.R: Adamu alipokuwa na umri wa miaka 130, alipata mtoto wa kiume aliyefanana naye, akamwita Sethi.

decisions.choice: in his likeness, according to his image: as Adam was made like God, Seth is like Adam
decisions.reason: The words of 1:26 return, in the other order. Adam passes on to his son the likeness he received from God: the image of God goes on in Adam's children (9:6).

decisions.choice: 130 years, as in the Hebrew text; the ages in this chapter differ in the ancient versions
decisions.reason: The ages at which the fathers have their sons differ between the Hebrew text, the Samaritan Pentateuch and the Septuagint. The Septuagint often adds a hundred years (230 here), and the Samaritan text differs for Jared, Methuselah and Lamech. The Hebrew numbers are followed throughout.

decisions.choice: long lifespans: the ages given in the text
decisions.reason: The men of this list live for centuries, and the ages fall after the flood (11:10-26) to the length of a life in later times (Psalm 90:10). Other ancient lists, such as the Sumerian King List, give far larger numbers for the rulers before the flood. The text gives the numbers without comment.

decisions.choice: 130 years
decisions.reason: Hebrew often gives the smaller number first ("thirty and a hundred years"). English says the larger first and, by the style of this translation, writes numbers over ninety-nine as numerals.

decisions.choice: fathered [a son]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "fathered" with no object until the name; Literal brackets "a son".

decisions.choice: 130 años; numbers over ninety-nine in numerals, smaller numbers in words ("noventa", "sesenta y cinco")
decisions.reason: As in English: the larger number comes first and, by the style of this translation, numbers over ninety-nine are written as numerals. The same holds for every age in this chapter.

decisions.choice: engendró (L); fue padre de / tuvo un hijo (B); tuvo un hijo (llamado ...) (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is the one used for a father "begetting" a child. Literal keeps "engendró", the standard Spanish word for it, with the personal "a" before a name. Balanced says "fue padre de" and Readable "tuvo un hijo llamado ..."; where the son is not named (5:3, 5:28) both say "tuvo un hijo". The same wording is used through the whole genealogy.

decisions.choice: le dio el nombre de Set
decisions.reason: At Literal the Hebrew "called his name" is kept as "llamó su nombre" only where the object is a group (5:2); for one person Spanish "le dio el nombre de" keeps the act of naming without the Hebraism.

decisions.choice: 130 ans; numbers over ninety-nine in figures, smaller numbers in words ("quatre-vingt-dix", "soixante-cinq")
decisions.reason: As the English, French gives the larger number first and writes the ages over ninety-nine in figures through the chapter, so the list can be read and compared at a glance.

decisions.choice: miaka 130; numbers over ninety-nine in figures, smaller numbers in words ("tisini", "sitini na tano")
decisions.reason: As the English, Swahili writes the ages over ninety-nine in figures through the chapter; the long Swahili number words ("mia tisa na kumi na mbili") would make the list hard to follow.

fr.R: Après la naissance de Seth, Adam a encore vécu 800 ans. Il a eu aussi d’autres fils et d’autres filles.

sw.R: Baada ya Sethi kuzaliwa, Adamu aliishi miaka 800 zaidi. Alipata pia watoto wengine wa kiume na wa kike.

decisions.choice: sons and daughters: many other children, unnamed
decisions.reason: Each father in the list has other sons and daughters besides the one named. The list follows one line; these other children explain where the people of 4:14-17 came from.

decisions.choice: después de engendrar a Set (L); Después del nacimiento de Set (B); Después de tener a Set (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses an infinitive ("after his fathering Seth"); Literal keeps the Spanish infinitive in the same place, between commas. Balanced uses a noun phrase and Readable a plain infinitive, which avoid the subjunctive that "después de que" calls for. The same pattern is used for every "after he fathered" in the chapter.

decisions.choice: and he died: the refrain of the list
decisions.reason: The words "and he died" close each life but one (verse 24), eight times in all. God's word in 2:17 and 3:19 has come true: however long they live, they die.

decisions.choice: Y fueron todos los días ... (L); En total, ... vivió (B); vivió hasta los ... años (R)
decisions.reason: The closing line of each entry: Literal keeps the Hebrew subject "all the days"; Balanced and Readable say how long the man lived, as the English does. Used for every entry in the chapter.

decisions.choice: Kenan: names like those in Cain's line
decisions.reason: Several names in this line resemble names in Cain's (4:17-18): Kenan and Cain, Jared and Irad, Enoch, Methuselah and Methushael, Lamech. The two lines are set side by side, and the two men named Enoch and Lamech are very different (4:23-24; 5:24, 29).

decisions.choice: Kénan

decisions.choice: walked with God: lived in close fellowship with God
decisions.reason: Where the formula says "lived", Enoch "walked with God". The verb form means to walk about, the form used of God walking in the garden (3:8); it is said again of Noah (6:9). It describes a life lived in God's company. The Septuagint translates it "pleased God", the wording Hebrews 11:5 follows.

decisions.choice: lived close to God
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m1).

decisions.choice: vivió muy unido a Dios
decisions.reason: As in English, Readable says what the idiom means (m1); "muy unido a" is the natural Spanish way to say "close to" a person, where "cerca de" suggests physical nearness.

decisions.reason: Spanish cannot say a bare "y no [era]"; "ya no estaba" keeps the Hebrew's understatement (m1) without saying how he left. Readable says "desapareció", as the English says "he was gone".

decisions.choice: Lamech: Noah's father, not the Lamech of 4:18-24
decisions.reason: This Lamech belongs to Seth's line. Where Cain's Lamech boasted of revenge (4:23-24), this one speaks of the hope of relief (verse 29).

records.literal_gloss: And he called his name Noah, saying, this [one] will comfort us from our work and from [the] painful toil of our hands, from the ground which has cursed YHWH.

en.L: And he called his name Noah, saying, "This one will comfort us in our work and in the painful toil of our hands, from the ground that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has cursed."
en.B: He named him Noah, saying, "He will bring us relief from our work and from the painful toil of our hands, caused by the ground that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has cursed."
en.R: He named him Noah. He said, "This boy will give us rest from our hard work, from all the hard labor we must do on the ground that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has cursed."

es.L: Y le dio el nombre de Noé, diciendo: «Este nos consolará en nuestro trabajo y en la dolorosa fatiga de nuestras manos, [a causa] del suelo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha maldecido».
es.B: Le puso por nombre Noé, y dijo: «Este nos dará alivio en nuestro trabajo y en la dura fatiga de nuestras manos, causada por el suelo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha maldecido».
es.R: Le puso por nombre Noé. Dijo: «Este niño nos dará descanso de nuestro duro trabajo, de todo lo que tenemos que trabajar en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha maldecido».

fr.L: Et il appela son nom Noé, disant : « Celui-ci nous consolera de notre travail et de la peine de nos mains, [qui vient] du sol que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a maudit. »
fr.B: Il l’appela Noé, en disant : « Il nous apportera du soulagement dans notre travail et dans la peine de nos mains, causée par le sol que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a maudit. »
fr.R: Il l’a appelé Noé. Il a dit : « Ce garçon nous donnera du repos dans notre travail pénible, dans tout ce dur labeur que nous devons faire sur la terre que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a maudite. »

sw.L: Naye akamwita jina lake Nuhu, akisema, "Huyu atatufariji katika kazi yetu na katika taabu ya mikono yetu, [itokayo] katika ardhi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameilaani."
sw.B: Akamwita Nuhu, akisema, "Yeye atatupumzisha kutoka katika kazi yetu na taabu ya mikono yetu, inayosababishwa na ardhi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameilaani."
sw.R: Akamwita Nuhu. Akasema, "Mtoto huyu atatupa pumziko kutoka katika kazi yetu ngumu, na kazi yote nzito tunayofanya katika ardhi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameilaani."

decisions.choice: Noah ... will comfort us: the name sounds like "rest" and "comfort"
decisions.reason: The name Noah (noach) sounds like the word for rest, and Lamech explains it with a verb of similar sound, "he will comfort us" (yenachamenu). The same verb returns in 6:6-7, where the LORD "regretted" that he had made humankind.

decisions.choice: painful toil ... the ground the LORD has cursed: the words of 3:17
decisions.reason: Lamech uses the words of God's judgment on the man: the cursed ground and painful toil (3:17). He hopes his son will bring relief from them. After the flood, Noah becomes a man of the soil who plants a vineyard (9:20), and God promises never again to curse the ground (8:21).

decisions.choice: el SEÑOR (default) / Yahvé (setting)
decisions.reason: The divine name: the default follows the tradition of reading "the LORD", in small capitals; the setting shows the name as "Yahvé". The span takes in the article and any contraction ("del SEÑOR" / "de Yahvé"). First occurrence in this chapter.

decisions.choice: [a causa] del suelo
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "from the ground": the toil comes from the cursed ground. Spanish "del suelo" alone would read as "of the ground", so Literal brackets "a causa". Literal and Balanced say "el suelo", as in 3:17, whose curse this verse recalls (see 2:5); Readable says "la tierra".

decisions.choice: a son of 500 years: 500 years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives age as "a son of" so many years.

decisions.choice: Shem, Ham and Japheth: the usual order, not necessarily the order of birth
decisions.reason: The three sons are always listed in this order (6:10; 10:1), but 9:24 calls Ham the youngest, and 10:21 may call Japheth the eldest. The verse does not say they were born in one year; 500 is when Noah began to have sons. The line now opens out into the peoples of chapter 10.
